steps.name: detailed_outline
steps.text:
1. Background
- core problem in traffic, economy, disease propagation analysis
- key challenge: complex temporal dynamics (non-stationary signal, periodicity)
- temporal dynamics = shape; e.g., traffic rush hour, abnormal electricity usage

2. Limits of existing work
- deep learning appealing but often inadequate for temporal dynamics
- Autoformer, FEDFormer: input sequence decomposition, but trained with L_{p} norm-based loss -> Fig. 1 (top)
- DTW for timely, accurate modeling of sudden changes; domain adversarial training for balanced (treatment invariant) representations
- still limited (Fig. 1 (middle)) -> shape needs more study

3. Shape and informative forecasting
- shape = pattern within a time interval: rise, drop, trough, peak, plateau
- informative prediction = models shape; invaluable for decision-making (e.g., economics)
- existing methods don't consider shape enough
- deep models take an easy learning path -> inaccurate, uninformative
- Fig. 1: Informer with different training metrics
- MSE: point-wise gap per time-step -> uninformative (Fig. 1 (top))
- gap + shape -> high accuracy, proper dynamics (Fig. 1 (bottom))
- need a loss for point-wise distance and shape

4. TILDE-Q
- objective guiding models to learn shapes
- review literature; concepts of shape and distortions (Sec. 3.1, 3.2, 3.3)
- necessary conditions for shape-aware objective (Sec. 4.1)
- TILDE-Q (Transformation Invariant Loss function with Distance EQualibrium): three distortion-invariant loss terms (Sec. 4.2)
- experiments with state-of-the-art models: model-agnostic; beats MSE and DILATE on MSE and shape metrics

## Contributions
- (1) shape awareness and distortion invariances in forecasting
- (2) TILDE-Q: invariant to three distortions, shape-aware, informative and timely forecasting
- (3) higher accuracy than models trained with MSE, DILATE

steps.name: rough_draft
steps.text:
Time-series forecasting has been a core problem in many domains, including the traffic domain, economy, and disease propagation analysis. One of the main challenges in time-series forecasting is modeling complex temporal dynamics (e.g., non-stationary signal and periodicity). Temporal dynamics, or intuitively shape, is the keyword that is emphasized most in time-series domains, like the rush hour in traffic data or abnormal usage of electricity.

Deep learning methods are an appealing solution for modeling complex non-linear temporal dependencies and nonstationary signals, but recent studies show that even deep learning is often not enough to model temporal dynamics. To model temporal dynamics properly, new deep learning approaches like Autoformer and FEDFormer have proposed decomposing the input sequence. But they are still trained with an L_{p} norm-based loss function, which cannot model the temporal dynamics properly, as shown in Fig. 1 (top). On the other hand, one work tries to model sudden changes in a timely and accurate way with dynamic time warping (DTW), and another uses domain adversarial training to learn balanced representations, which are treatment invariant representations over time. These two try to capture the shape but they still have some limitations, as shown in Fig. 1 (middle), which means the shape needs to be investigated further.

Identifying shape, meaning the pattern in time-series data within a given time interval, is important for addressing the limitation mentioned above in the time-series forecasting problem. Shape can give valuable information such as rise, drop, trough, peak, and plateau. We call a prediction informative when it can model the shape appropriately. In real-world applications, including economics, informative prediction is invaluable for making decisions. To get this kind of informative forecasting, a model should take shape into account instead of only trying to forecast the accurate value for each time step. However, existing methods do not consider the shape enough. Also, deep learning models tend to choose an easy learning path, which gives inaccurate and uninformative forecasting results that ignore the characteristics of time-series data. Fig. 1 shows three real forecasting results we got with Informer and different training metrics. When the mean squared error (MSE) is the objective, the model tries to reduce the gap between prediction and ground truth for each time-step. This "point-wise" distance-based optimization is less able to model shape, so it generates uninformative predictions regardless of the temporal dynamics (Fig. 1 (top)), and the model rarely gives information about the time-series. In contrast, if both the gap and the shape of the prediction and ground truth are taken into account, the model can get high accuracy with proper temporal dynamics, as in Fig. 1 (bottom). So time-series forecasting needs a loss function that considers both point-wise distance (i.e., the traditional goal) and shape.

In this work we aim to design a new objective function that guides models to improve forecasting performance by learning shapes in time-series data. To design a shape-aware loss function, we review existing literature and explore the concepts of shapes and of distortions that prevent appropriate measurement of similarity between two time-series data in terms of shape (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 3.2, and Sec. 3.3). Based on this investigation, we propose necessary conditions for building an objective function for shape-aware time-series forecasting (Sec. 4.1). Then we present a new loss function, TILDE-Q (Transformation Invariant Loss function with Distance EQualibrium), which allows shape-aware representation learning by using three loss terms that are invariant to distortions (Sec. 4.2). For evaluation, we do extensive experiments with state-of-the-art deep learning models with TILDE-Q. The results show that TILDE-Q is model-agnostic and outperforms MSE and DILATE in MSE and shape-related metrics.

## Contributions

To summarize, our study makes these contributions. (1) We look into the concept of shape awareness and distortion invariances in time-series forecasting. By investigating these distortions thoroughly, we understand better how they impact time-series forecasting problems. (2) We propose and implement TILDE-Q, which has invariances to three distortions and achieves shape-awareness, making informative forecasting possible in a timely manner. (3) We show empirically that TILDE-Q lets models get higher accuracy than models trained with other existing metrics, such as MSE and DILATE.

steps.text:

One of the key challenges in time-series forecasting is modeling complex temporal dynamics (e.g., non-stationary signal and periodicity). Temporal dynamics, intuitively shape, is the most emphasized keyword in time-series domains, such as the rush hour of traffic data or abnormal usage of electricity [5,6,7,8,9].

Although deep learning methods are an appealing solution for modeling complex non-linear temporal dependencies and nonstationary signals, recent studies have revealed that even deep learning is often inadequate for modeling temporal dynamics. To properly model temporal dynamics, novel deep learning approaches such as Autoformer [8] and FEDFormer [9] have proposed input sequence decomposition. Still, they are trained with an L_{p} norm-based loss function, which cannot properly model the temporal dynamics, as shown in Fig. 1 (top). On the other hand, [10] attempt to model sudden changes in a timely and accurate manner with dynamic time warping (DTW), and [11] adopt domain adversarial training to learn balanced representations, i.e., treatment invariant representations over time. [10,11] try to capture the shape but still have limitations, as depicted in Fig. 1 (middle), implying that the shape needs further investigation.

Identifying shape, the pattern in time-series data within a given time interval, plays an important role in addressing the aforementioned limitation in the time-series forecasting problem. Shape can provide valuable information such as rise, drop, trough, peak, and plateau. We refer to a prediction as informative when it appropriately models the shape. In real-world applications, including economics, informative prediction is invaluable for decision-making. To achieve such informative forecasting, a model should account for shape instead of solely aiming to forecast an accurate value for each time step. However, existing methods inadequately consider the shape [8,9,11,10]. Moreover, deep learning models tend to opt for an easy learning path [12], yielding inaccurate and uninformative forecasting results that disregard the characteristics of time-series data. Fig. 1 illustrates three real forecasting results obtained with Informer [13] and different training metrics. When the mean squared error (MSE) is used as the objective, the model aims to reduce the gap between prediction and ground truth at each time-step. This "point-wise" distance-based optimization is less able to model shape, resulting in uninformative predictions regardless of temporal dynamics (Fig. 1 (top)); the model rarely provides information about the time-series. In contrast, if both the gap and the shape of the prediction and ground truth are taken into account, the model can achieve high accuracy with proper temporal dynamics, as shown in Fig. 1 (bottom). Consequently, time-series forecasting requires a loss function that considers both point-wise distance (i.e., the traditional goal) and shape.

In this work, we aim to design a novel objective function that guides models to improve forecasting performance by learning shapes in time-series data. To design a shape-aware loss function, we review existing literature [14,6,15] and explore the concepts of shapes and of the distortions that impede appropriate measurement of similarity between two time-series data in terms of shape (Sec. 3.1, Sec. 3.2, and Sec. 3.3). We then present a novel loss function, TILDE-Q (Transformation Invariant Loss function with Distance EQualibrium), which enables shape-aware representation learning through three loss terms that are invariant to distortions (Sec. 4.2). For evaluation, we conduct extensive experiments with state-of-the-art deep learning models trained with TILDE-Q. The results indicate that TILDE-Q is model-agnostic and outperforms MSE and DILATE in MSE and shape-related metrics.

In summary, our study makes the following contributions. (1) We delve into the concept of shape awareness and distortion invariances in time-series forecasting. By thoroughly investigating these distortions, we deepen our understanding of their impact on time-series forecasting problems. (2) We propose and implement TILDE-Q, which is invariant to three distortions and achieves shape-awareness, enabling informative forecasting in a timely manner. (3) We empirically demonstrate that TILDE-Q allows models to achieve higher accuracy than models trained with other existing metrics, such as MSE and DILATE.
